sentences.text:
The present petition has been remanded to this court,
inter alia, to consider the objections raised by the respondents regarding filing of the present petition.
It is the DDA's case that the present petition was filed by suppressing the facts, as it was not instituted by the recorded owners of the subject land.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 11/03/2025 at 21:23:05 3.

The petitioners had filed the above-captioned petition seeking a declaration that the subject lands owned by them, lands comprising in Khasra No.190 (4-16) and 116 (4-16) measuring 9 bighas and 12 biswas situated in Village Satbari, Delhi had lapsed by virtue of Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Ram Phal And Ors vs Uoi And Ors on 5 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28731468/
1 Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereafter the 2013 Act).
As noted above, this petition was allowed by a judgment dated 23.08.2016.

The Delhi Development Authority (DDA) had appealed the said decision, which was considered by the Supreme Court in a batch of matters along with Civil Appeal No.6798/2024.
4.
The present petition was listed on 28.10.2024 pursuant to the orders passed by the Supreme Court.
On that date, none was present on behalf of the petitioners and accordingly, court notice was issued to the petitioners.
5. Pursuant to the said notice, Mr Hari Prakash has appeared and he states that he is the son of petitioner no.4 (Sh. Vishamber).
He states that petitioner no.4 had expired in in December 2009.
He also states that petitioner nos.3 and 5 had also expired prior to institution of the present petition.
Petitioner no.1 (Sh. Ram Phal) has since expired in the year 2024.
It is noticed that the present petition was filed by one Sh. Punit Sabharwal son of Sh. R.C. Sabharwal, who claimed to be the power of attorney holder of the petitioners' land.

It is also noticed that copy of the power of attorney,
which is executed by one Sh. B.D. Bhatt on 27.01.2015, has been annexed with the present petition.
6. In addition to the said power of attorney, the petitioners have also enclosed the power of attorney dated 10.08.2009 executed by one Sh. Sanjay Gupta in favour of Sh. B.D. Bhatt.
The said power of attorney indicates that This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 11/03/2025 at 21:23:05 Sh. B.D. Bhatt was constituted as an attorney by the petitioners in respect of part of the subject land.

7. It is, thus, according to the submission made by Mr. Hari Prakash, apparent that the said power of attorneys were invalid as petitioner nos.3 to 5 had since expired and this fact was not informed to this court.
8. In view of the above, we find merit in the contention advanced on behalf of the respondents.
The present petition has been filed by suppression of material facts and is liable to be dismissed on the said ground alone.
9. In view of the above, the present petition is dismissed.
10. We, however, clarify that this would not preclude the petitioners/their legal heirs from availing their remedies, if any, in accordance with law.
